name: Dark Grey Blue
lede: Dark grey blue is a descriptive name for a deep, slate-leaning blue, and one dictionary uses the phrase to define Flemish blue.

sections.title: A shade, described
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary of colour defines Flemish blue as a rich or dark grey-blue [1]. Flemish blue is therefore an older name for the territory this swatch covers, and the plain words dark grey blue are a modern descriptive label for it. The dictionary entry gives no date for the name, and its origin in our books is undocumented.

On screen the swatch is a dark, cool blue with a touch of green and grey, sitting near [[slate-grey]], [[steel-blue]], [[navy]] and [[midnight-blue]]. The color is also an easy one to mistake for black in dim light, and seeing the blue in it is the useful skill.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This swatch appears in 242 of 23,781 paintings, 1.02 per cent [2]. It peaks in the 1400s, in 10 of 945 paintings, 1.6 times the museums' baseline [2]. In 54 per cent of the 125 paintings where it is measured inside the picture, it is a hidden color [2]. The numbers are as photographed, and the dark of an aged varnish can turn many dark blues into this one.
